title: The Last Signal from Orbit Nine
synopsis: A junior satellite engineer receives a distress call from a spacecraft decommissioned years earlier.

chapters.title: The Unexpected Message
paragraphs: The message from Orbit Nine arrived eleven minutes after the station went silent. It contained four words: DO NOT TRUST AUTOMATION. On Earth, the rescue team had already handed control to an AI.

The first sign was so small that most people would have mistaken it for a printing error. Aya Chen, a satellite systems engineer had come to a communications center above the winter clouds expecting routine work. Instead, Aya Chen found a signal packet signed by a retired spacecraft. The object was ordinary enough to fit in a pocket, yet it did not belong to the place or the hour. That contradiction would prove more important than the object itself.

Rafi, an onboard maintenance intelligence had a different interpretation. "A clue only tells us where to look," Rafi said, "not what to believe." Aya Chen wrote down the observation before answering. The people around them were eager for a quick conclusion, but a conclusion reached too early could make an innocent person carry the blame.

Commander Solis, the station's skeptical director pointed out a detail the others had missed. The detail connected the day's discovery to a decision that nobody had questioned for years. It was tempting to call the connection a coincidence. Instead, they compared dates, asked careful questions, and listened to the answers even when the answers complicated their plan.

Introduce the characters and the unusual clue that disturbs an ordinary day. Their investigation returned again to a signal packet signed by a retired spacecraft. What had seemed like a single mystery was also a story about trust: who kept records, who was believed, and who had been left out. Aya Chen realized that finding the truth would not be enough unless they considered what would happen after telling it.

As the day ended, Aya Chen and Rafi made a practical decision. They would preserve the evidence, speak to the people most affected, and resist the pressure to turn uncertainty into accusation. The choice did not solve everything, but it gave them a way to continue without betraying the reason they had started.
